Ozeryany New Jewish Cemetery (Volyn Region)

Jewish Cemetery · Ozeriany, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's founding is undocumented, presumably existing by the early 20th century, appearing on prewar maps; a neighbor recalls the cemetery's existence and many gravestones once present on the site. Jews are first recorded in Ozeriany in the early 18th century; the Council of the Four Lands held its only Volyn meeting here in 1761. Sources vary on population by 1820 (either 706 or 340); population reached about 850 by 1941. Nazi occupation began June 28, 1941; a ghetto formed in spring 1942, holding local and surrounding-village Jews. NOTE: the source's own text gives 'August 1941' for the ghetto's liquidation, which appears to be an error given the ghetto itself is described as forming in spring 1942 - the more chronologically consistent date would be August 1942, when 762 Jews were shot near the Sushibaba cemetery. Only six Ozeriany Jews survived WWII. A 1989 monument marks the shooting site.
